sourceReview.detail: Instructor notice printed 'Tomorrow's section (22/10/2026)'; per department correction the Basic Pharmacology section is 22/11/2026 (Sunday). Encoded on 2026-11-22.
Normal A/B weekly alternation suspended this date: BOTH halves attend, at split rooms (A: Wet Lab 7F New; B: Lecture Hall 6F New).

The notice states no clock time. The standing weekly (pharmd-s5-basic-pharmacology-practical, every-week-all-groups) already marks every Y3 group busy across 09:00–14:50 on 22/11, so a timed override would add no busy correctness and would BORROW the weekly bands — placing the B-half at the same time as the Drug Information w10 Group-B tutorial (e.g. Group 1-B 11:00–12:50 in both) and manufacturing a phantom cross-course clash. Therefore encoded allDay=true: compare.js busy math ignores all-day events (timedEventsOnDate filters !allDay), so no false busy/free, no polluted common-free-windows, no DI collision, while the room split and both-halves attendance remain visible in the all-day strip.

CI fix: the validator asserts every session carries a group. The first draft used a single session with group:null (the all-day banner needs no per-group timing), which failed with 'session missing group'. The notice genuinely applies to every Y3 practical group's both halves, so it now carries three group-tagged sessions (1, 2, 3) with subdivision omitted (⇒ both A and B) and start/end null under allDay=true. The engine builds the all-day occurrence from the event date and uses the session rows only for group/subdivision filtering, so the null times are never read as intervals — same convention as the timed both-halves DI w11 event, minus the times, plus allDay.

The standing weekly encodes Basic Pharmacology with no A/B subdivisions, yet this notice speaks of A and B halves at two rooms. The A/B structure (and which numbered groups' halves are A vs B) is not resolvable from any supplied source; the notice's room split is recorded here as metadata, not as a resolved per-subdivision timed schedule.

No seat ranges or practical-group numbers are printed (unlike the ChemSketch/Organic batch sheets), so 'group A and B' is read as the course-wide A/B halves applying to every Y3 practical group; the event is unfiltered within the semester-5 (Y3) dataset, so its blast radius is Y3 only.
